title: Relative Homology Excision and Mayer Vietoris

items.title: Relative singular chain complex
items.strategy: For a fixed abelian coefficient group G, define C_*(X,A;G)=C_*(X;G)/C_*(A;G) for A subset X, with finite chains.

items.title: Boundary on relative chains
items.strategy: Use preservation of C_*(A) by the singular boundary to descend the differential and square it to zero.

items.title: Relative singular homology
items.strategy: Define H_n(X,A) as the homology of the quotient chain complex and state its cycle-with-boundary-in-A interpretation.

items.title: Functoriality of relative homology
items.strategy: Descend the induced singular chain map for f(A) subset B and pass to homology.

items.title: Relative homology for the empty and total subspace
items.strategy: Identify the quotient chain complex for A empty and A=X, including degree zero.

items.title: Long exact sequence of a pair
items.strategy: Apply the homological-algebra long exact sequence to 0 to C_*(A) to C_*(X) to C_*(X,A) to 0.

items.title: Relative connecting homomorphism on cycles
items.strategy: For a relative cycle, take its ordinary boundary in A and fix the sign convention displayed by the pair sequence.

items.title: Well-definedness of the relative connector
items.strategy: Compare two lifts and two representatives in the quotient complex, tracking the induced A-boundaries.

items.title: Naturality of the pair long exact sequence
items.strategy: Use the commuting morphism of short exact singular-chain sequences and identify the relative connector chainwise.

items.title: Barycenter and affine cone
items.strategy: Set the ordered-simplex and cone orientation conventions that determine subdivision signs.

items.title: Barycentric subdivision operator
items.strategy: Define S recursively by coning the subdivided boundary, with S on zero-simplices equal to the identity.

items.title: Barycentric subdivision is a chain map
items.strategy: Prove the cone-boundary identity and induct on simplex dimension to show partial S equals S partial.

items.title: Subdivision prism homotopy
items.strategy: Define T recursively from the cone operator so its degree is raised by one.

items.title: Subdivision is chain homotopic to the identity
items.strategy: Verify partial T plus T partial equals 1 minus S by induction, preserving the stated sign convention.

items.title: Mesh tends to zero under iterated subdivision
items.strategy: Establish the dimension-dependent contraction estimate for affine simplices, then iterate it.

items.title: Cover-small singular chains
items.strategy: For a family whose interiors cover X, define the subcomplex generated by simplices carried by one member.

items.title: Finite chains eventually become cover-small
items.strategy: For the finite union of simplex images, use a Lebesgue number and take the finite maximum of the least subdivision depths in ZF.

items.title: Cover-small chains compute singular homology
items.strategy: Use chainwise subdivision depths for surjectivity and the prism identity for injectivity; do not assert a uniform depth for all simplices.

items.title: The cover-small inclusion is a chain-homotopy equivalence
items.strategy: Construct the small-chain retraction and both homotopies using compatible finite subdivision choices.

items.title: Excision for singular homology
items.strategy: With closure Z inside interior A, compare cover-small quotient complexes for (X-Z,A-Z) and (X,A).

items.title: Good pairs and quotient reduced homology
items.strategy: Use excision around A and the quotient comparison for a good pair, handling the reduced degree-zero convention explicitly.

items.title: Cover-small chains for a two-open cover
items.strategy: For U and V with open interiors covering X, partition each small simplex by the member containing it and identify the intersection.

items.title: Short exact chain Mayer–Vietoris sequence
items.strategy: Prove exactness of 0 to C(U cap V) to C(U) direct-sum C(V) to C(X) to 0 with the fixed difference sign.

items.title: Mayer–Vietoris sequence in singular homology
items.strategy: Apply the chain long exact sequence to the small complexes and transfer through the cover-small homology isomorphisms.

items.title: Mayer–Vietoris connecting class
items.strategy: For a cycle decomposed as u plus v, define the connector by the class of partial u, with the sequence’s sign convention.

items.title: Well-definedness of the Mayer–Vietoris connector
items.strategy: Subtract two decompositions, use exactness at the direct sum, and pass the resulting common boundary to homology.

items.title: Naturality of singular Mayer–Vietoris
items.strategy: Use a map preserving the chosen two-set covers to form a natural morphism of short exact small-chain sequences.

items.title: Simplicial and singular homology agree
items.strategy: Construct the natural simplicial-to-singular comparison and use local simplex acyclicity, skeletal induction, and the five lemma.

items.title: Homology of spheres
items.strategy: Apply comparison to the boundary of a simplex, state reduced and unreduced groups, and keep S^0 separate.

items.title: Suspension isomorphism in reduced singular homology
items.strategy: Apply reduced Mayer–Vietoris to the two cones, state the based well-pointed qualification, and identify the degree shift.

title: Relative Homology Excision and Mayer Vietoris — Examples

items.title: Relative homology of a disk and its boundary
items.strategy: Compute H_*(D^n,S^{n-1}), display the boundary isomorphism and fix the relative fundamental-class convention.

items.title: Relative homology of an interval and its endpoints
items.strategy: Use the pair sequence for ([0,1],{0,1}) to exhibit the generator and its signed endpoint boundary.

items.title: First barycentric subdivision of a triangle
items.strategy: Write the six oriented small triangles and check their interior-edge cancellation against the boundary convention.

items.title: Cover-small chains for a two-arc cover of a circle
items.strategy: Choose two overlapping arcs and exhibit a finite subdivided cycle together with a valid small-chain decomposition.

items.title: Mayer–Vietoris computation of sphere homology
items.strategy: Use two contractible hemispherical opens and their equatorial overlap, spelling out the reduced degree-zero base case.

items.title: Mayer–Vietoris computation of first homology of the torus
items.strategy: Use product cylinders whose intersection has two circle components; calculate the two relevant maps and obtain H_1(T^2;G) as G direct-sum G.

items.title: Excision fails without closure inside interior
items.strategy: With Z coefficients, use X=[0,1], A=Z={0}; compare H_0((0,1],empty) with H_0([0,1],{0}) to show the boundary-point omission fails.

items.title: No uniform subdivision depth for all singular simplices
items.strategy: For each proposed depth construct a continuous zigzag simplex crossing the chosen two-set cover within one depth-sized subsimplex.

items.title: Relative homology is not homology of the set difference
items.strategy: With Z coefficients and n at least two, compare H_n(D^n,S^{n-1}) with H_n(D^n minus S^{n-1}), the latter being an open ball.
